novelty.justification: The claim hypothesizes that errors arise because "the fact is encoded in mid-layer representations but never gets copied into the residual stream at the answer position," pairing a storage-versus-retrieval distinction with an activation intervention. Searches around "stored knowledge retrieval failure answer extraction hallucinations," "knows fact but fails to use internal probes," and "factual recall pipeline restoration" surfaced the closest work, Mechanistic Understanding and Mitigation of Language Model Non-Factual Hallucinations (EMNLP 2024), which already distinguishes insufficient lower-layer knowledge from upper-layer answer-extraction failure and mitigates errors by targeted restoration of the internal fact-recall pipeline. The proposed example-level classifier and "retrieval nudge" are incremental operational variants of that established mechanism rather than a new core relationship, so the hypothesis is essentially a direct transfer with limited novelty.
